subject.title: Add Herdr state bridge for OpenClaw TUI

question: Should Herdr pane-state reporting be owned as a bundled plugin-gated capability, explicit core TUI behavior, or kept outside OpenClaw core?
rationale: The current diff mixes a default-on bundled plugin wrapper with a core TUI env-triggered sidecar, and automation should not choose the permanent ownership/API boundary for an optional external integration.

options.title: Gate Through Plugin Policy
options.body: Treat `herdr-state` as the owner and start the sidecar only after resolved plugin policy confirms the plugin is enabled and allowed.

options.title: Make It Core-Owned
options.body: Remove the misleading plugin wrapper and document `HERDR_PANE_ID` as an explicit core TUI integration with maintainer-accepted env behavior.

options.title: Move Outside Core
options.body: Close or pause this PR until a generic TUI status seam or external Herdr package can own the integration without bundled core behavior.

recommendation.title: Gate Through Plugin Policy
recommendation.body: Treat `herdr-state` as the owner and start the sidecar only after resolved plugin policy confirms the plugin is enabled and allowed.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans TUI lifecycle behavior and plugin-policy docs, both areas with recent `steipete` ownership signals.
